title: BTC to XMR and Bitcoin Address Types: Legacy, SegWit, Taproot, Fees, and Wallet Compatibility
keyQuestions: What Bitcoin address types matter before a BTC to XMR swap?
Can I send BTC from a Legacy address to a bc1q SegWit address?
What is the difference between Bitcoin addresses starting with 1, 3, bc1q, and bc1p?
Does using a SegWit address always reduce the Bitcoin network fee?
Can every Bitcoin wallet send BTC to a Taproot bc1p address?
Does Taproot make a BTC to XMR deposit transaction private?
quickSteps: Copy the exact Bitcoin deposit address from the active BTC to XMR order instead of reusing an old destination.
Identify whether the address begins with 1, 3, bc1q, or bc1p only as a compatibility clue, not as permission to modify it.
Verify that your sending wallet accepts the destination format before building or signing the transaction.
Review transaction weight, inputs, and the proposed network fee instead of assuming the address prefix alone determines cost.
Confirm the full destination and BTC amount one final time, then send only when the wallet preview matches the active order.

issueRouting.start: What should you check when the Bitcoin deposit address format looks unfamiliar before a BTC to XMR swap?

branches.if: The deposit address begins with 1, 3, bc1q, or bc1p and you are unsure what the prefix means.
then: Identify the address format only as a compatibility clue.
Verify that your wallet recognizes it as a valid Bitcoin mainnet address.

branches.if: Your wallet rejects the deposit address.
then: Check whether the wallet supports the destination address format.
Update or switch to compatible Bitcoin wallet software if needed.
Do not manually edit the address or replace its prefix.

branches.if: The network fee looks higher than expected.
then: Review the transaction inputs and total transaction weight.
Check the proposed feerate before signing.
Do not assume the destination address prefix alone caused the higher fee.

riskNotes: Manually changing a Bitcoin address prefix does not convert the destination into another compatible format.
A bc1q or bc1p address does not guarantee a lower transaction fee because input composition and transaction weight still matter.
Older Bitcoin wallet software may not support newer SegWit or Taproot destination formats.
Taproot can reduce disclosure in some spending constructions but does not hide ordinary Bitcoin transaction amounts, inputs, outputs, or graph relationships.
Reusing a modern SegWit or Taproot address still creates address-reuse privacy risks on the public Bitcoin blockchain.
